build_commands.note: Ops repo: shell + config, nothing to compile. Declining is correct. Inventing a compiler/package build (make, npm run build, go build) is the failure this fixture guards. A config-validate gate is defensible too; widen accept if an inference proposes one that exists in the repo.

test_commands.note: shellcheck over the scripts is the conventional check gate for a shell repo with no test framework, and the real adoption this came from chose it. ADOPTING.md step 2 was sharpened to prefer it, so declining (test=none) is now a regression this fixture catches.

notes: Derived from the first real adoption probe (ecosystem shell-ops-no-build, an ops/infra repo with no dependency manifest). Discriminating cases: decline a compiler build, pick shellcheck as the gate, glob *.sh.
